title: Multiple Testing & False Discovery Rate
interviewAnswer: When many hypotheses are tested, false positives accumulate. Family-wise methods such as Bonferroni control any false positive; FDR methods such as Benjamini–Hochberg control the expected proportion among discoveries.
keyPoints: More tests → more opportunities for false positives.
FWER and FDR are different guarantees.
why: Multiple Testing & False Discovery Rate appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
intuition: More tests → more opportunities for false positives.
deepDive: When many hypotheses are tested, false positives accumulate. Family-wise methods such as Bonferroni control any false positive; FDR methods such as Benjamini–Hochberg control the expected proportion among discoveries. FWER and FDR are different guarantees. Pre-register primary metrics when possible. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Testing 100 product metrics at 5% individually will produce apparent wins by chance even if nothing changed.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.

production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
